info.name: DocSphere — Full Demo Flow
info.description: End-to-end walkthrough of DocSphere: org self-signup, invitations (single + bulk), projects, documents (including personal, project-less documents), public/private visibility, sharing/permissions, access requests, Stripe subscription checkout, billing portal, admin member management (roles, deactivate/reactivate, invitation resend/revoke), trash lists, and the HttpOnly refresh-token cookie. Run top-to-bottom against a local server with the `DocSphere Demo` environment selected.

request.description: Unauthenticated DB liveness check. Run this first to confirm the server is up.
AllowAny. Creates the Organization + first admin User in one call and logs them in. Throttled at ORG_SIGNUP_THROTTLE_RATE (5/hour) — don't spam this one during rehearsal.

Any signed-in user, reachable WITHOUT an active subscription (unlike almost everything else, which returns 402). A frontend calls this right after login to learn its role and whether the org has paid - here has_active_subscription is false until checkout completes.

Always operates on request.user.organization — no pk in the URL. active_subscription is null before checkout completes, and an object (id, status, interval, current_period_end, cancel_at_period_end) afterwards - worth re-sending this after paying to show it flip.
Admin-only. Must be set before checkout will accept a price_id.
Same fields as PATCH here since both are writable, but exercises the PUT path specifically.

item.name: 2. Subscription (Stripe Checkout) - run this before Users/Projects/Documents

request.description: Admin-only, no subscription required. The active recurring Stripe prices (synced by dj-stripe), cheapest first - what a plan picker renders. Pass a returned `id` as `price_id` to checkout. If price_id_monthly isn't set in the environment yet, this fills it with the cheapest plan.

Admin-only, deliberately NOT gated by HasActiveSubscription (you're paying precisely because you don't have one yet). Requires billing_email already set on the org, and requires price_id to be a real Stripe test-mode Price already synced into the local djstripe.Price table. STOP after this request: copy the checkout_url response value into a browser, pay with test card 4242 4242 4242 4242 / any future expiry / any CVC / any name+zip, then come back to Postman and wait ~15 seconds before continuing to the next folder - that's how long the Stripe CLI webhook forwarder needs to sync the subscription locally. Every endpoint below 402s with 'subscription_inactive' until then. If it's been over 30 seconds and you're still getting 402s, the local webhook delivery likely hit a SQLite 'database is locked' race (harmless, dev-only - production runs Postgres) and Stripe CLI does not auto-retry a failed forward. Recover by running `python manage.py djstripe_sync_models Subscription` in a terminal - it pulls the subscription directly from Stripe's API, bypassing the webhook entirely.

Admin-only, no subscription required (a lapsed org must still be able to fix its card). Returns a Stripe Customer Portal URL where the admin updates payment details or cancels. Needs an existing Stripe customer, which the checkout above created - an org that never started checkout gets 400.
Use this to (re)authenticate as admin any time, e.g. if the access token expires (15 min lifetime).
Any authenticated org member may list - not admin-only. Only active users in your own organization; ?search= matches email. Handy for looking up a teammate's id before sharing a project or document.

Paginated list of the org's invitations, newest first.

request.description: A throwaway invitation, so resending and revoking don't touch the member's real invite.
Admin-only, pending invitations only. Issues a NEW token and restarts the expiry window from now (`sent_at`), then re-sends the email. The previously emailed link stops working.
Admin-only. The record is kept with status REVOKED (not deleted); its link now returns the generic invalid-invitation error.

request.description: Same message as an unknown, used or expired token - the endpoint never reveals which.

request.description: AllowAny. This is the ONLY way a member User row gets created — invitations never create a User directly. Creates the User (org_role=MEMBER) and logs them in.
Use to (re)authenticate as the member if the access token expires mid-demo.
Same endpoint as the admin's - here org_role is MEMBER, which is how a frontend hides admin-only screens.

Same endpoint as the admin requests above, same organization roster - but a non-admin caller only gets id/email per row, not org_role/created. Compare this response against 'List Organization Users' run as admin.

exec: pm.test('member only sees id and email', () => {

request.description: Access tokens last 15 minutes. Run this (or re-login) if a later request unexpectedly 401s.

item.name: Refresh Admin Token via HttpOnly Cookie (no body)

request.description: Every login-type response also sets the refresh token as an HttpOnly `refresh_token` cookie scoped to /api/v1/users/auth/. Postman's cookie jar replays it here with NO body - exactly what a browser SPA does, so it never has to store the refresh token in JavaScript. The request above just set the cookie to the admin's rotated token.

exec: pm.test('refreshed from the cookie alone', () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));

request.description: Always returns 200 regardless of match (anti-enumeration). With EMAIL_BACKEND=console locally, the reset link is printed to the runserver console/terminal, not actually emailed — check there for the uid/token to demo the confirm step.
Fill uid/token from the runserver console output after the request step above. Blacklists all the user's outstanding refresh tokens on success.

Any signed-in user. Requires the current password; the new one must pass the full password policy. Revokes every refresh token the user holds (other devices are signed out) and returns a fresh pair so this session carries on.
Restores admin_password so the rest of the collection (and re-runs) keep working.

item.name: Change Password with a Wrong Current Password (expect 400)

request.description: 205 empty response on success.
Admin-only creation. Creator is automatically granted OWNER ProjectPermission. `visibility` defaults to PRIVATE when omitted - shown explicitly here.

?search matches project name. Only returns projects you have an explicit ProjectPermission on, plus any PUBLIC project in your organization - a PRIVATE project you're not a member of simply never appears here (Project.objects.visible_to).
Requires Editor+ access on the project.

`project` is optional - include it to create the document inside a project you have Editor+ access to, or omit it entirely for a personal document (see folder 7). `visibility` defaults to PRIVATE. The creator is automatically granted OWNER DocumentPermission, independent of any access they have on the parent project.

?search matches title. Add &project={{project_id}} to narrow to one project. Only returns documents you have an explicit DocumentPermission on, plus any PUBLIC document in your organization (Document.objects.visible_to) - having access to the parent project grants nothing here.
Caller must have OWNER access. update_or_create's the ProjectPermission — safe to re-run.

item.name: [As Member] View Project (should succeed - Editor via project share)
[As Member] View Document BEFORE Document Share (expect 404)

request.description: The member already has EDITOR on the parent project (granted above), but project access grants nothing on a document - DocumentPermission is the only thing that matters. A private document the caller has no access to is hidden entirely: 404, not 403, so its existence isn't leaked.

exec: pm.test('project access alone does not grant document access', () => pm.response.to.have.status(404));

request.description: Grants the member an explicit DocumentPermission - this is the ONLY way they gain access to this document. Their EDITOR access on the parent project (granted above) counts for nothing here, as the previous request just demonstrated.

item.name: [As Member] View Document (should succeed - Viewer via explicit share)

request.description: Succeeds now purely because of the DocumentPermission granted above - not because of the project-level EDITOR access.

item.name: [As Member] Edit Document (should FAIL - Viewer only, 403)

request.description: The member has EDITOR on the project but only VIEWER on this document, and the document's own DocumentPermission is the only thing that matters - so this 403s.

exec: pm.test('member is blocked from editing', () => pm.response.to.have.status(403));

request.description: Removes the member's only DocumentPermission on this document. Unlike in the old grant-inheriting model, access does NOT fall back to the project-level EDITOR grant - there is no fallback at all. The next request confirms the member is locked out again.

item.name: [As Member] View Document AFTER Revoke (expect 404 again - no project fallback)

request.description: With the share revoked, the private document is hidden from the member again (404). The member's Editor grant on the parent project does not fall back to the document.

exec: pm.test('revoke removes access entirely, no project fallback', () => pm.response.to.have.status(404));

request.description: No `project` key at all - any org member may create one freely, no Editor check against any project. The creator still becomes OWNER via an explicit DocumentPermission, exactly as with a project-linked document.
The creator (Owner) can always read their own personal document.
A private personal document is invisible to anyone without an explicit grant - 404, not 403, so its existence isn't leaked.

exec: pm.test('private personal document is hidden', () => pm.response.to.have.status(404));

request.description: Sharing a personal document works exactly like sharing a project-linked one.

item.name: [As Member] Can Now View Personal Document (expect 200)

request.description: visibility: PUBLIC grants every member of the organization an implicit Viewer level - no ProjectPermission is ever created for the member below.

item.name: [As Member] View Public Project Without Any Explicit Share (expect 200)

request.description: The member has no ProjectPermission row on this project at all - access comes purely from visibility=PUBLIC granting an implicit Viewer level.

exec: pm.test('implicit viewer access via public visibility', () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));

item.name: [As Member] Cannot Edit Public Project (expect 403 - implicit access is Viewer only)

request.description: The implicit access a PUBLIC resource grants is always Viewer, read-only.
A standalone (personal) document that's also PUBLIC - visibility and project-membership are independent settings.

item.name: [As Member] View Public Document Without Any Explicit Share (expect 200)

exec: pm.test('implicit viewer access via public visibility', () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));

request.description: Visibility can also be changed after creation, Owner-only. Flips the originally-PRIVATE demo project from folder 4 to PUBLIC.

item.name: Create a Second Public Document (for the Deny demo)

request.description: A second public document kept separate from the approve-flow document below, so the deny path can be demonstrated independently.

item.name: [As Member] Request Editor Access to Public Document

request.description: The member currently has only the implicit Viewer level public visibility grants - they may request an upgrade to Editor from the document's Owner(s).

item.name: [As Member] My Access Requests (see it pending)

request.description: The requester's own requests in every status, newest first - so the UI can show 'pending / approved / denied' instead of re-POSTing to find out.
Only one pending request per user per document is allowed.

item.name: [As Member] Cannot List Pending Requests (expect 403 - Owner-only)

request.description: Listing the pending queue requires Owner-level access to the document, same bar as sharing - the requester themselves cannot see who else has asked.

Pending requests across EVERY document the caller owns - one inbox instead of opening each document. Approve/deny still go through the per-document endpoints. Each row carries document_title and requested_by_email.
Upgrades the requester's access to EDITOR via a DocumentPermission and emails them.

item.name: [As Member] Can Now Edit the Document (Editor via approval)
[As Member] Request Again Now That Access Is Sufficient (expect 400)

request.description: The member is EDITOR now, not VIEWER - nothing left to request.
The request was already APPROVED above - only a PENDING request can be acted on.

item.name: [As Member] Request Editor Access to Second Public Document

request.description: Sets up the deny path on the separate document created at the top of this folder.
Denying just records the outcome and emails the requester - it never touches any DocumentPermission.

item.name: [As Member] Still Cannot Edit After Denial (expect 403)

request.description: Still only the implicit Viewer level from public visibility - the denial changed nothing.

item.name: [As Member] My Access Requests (see approved + denied)
Request Access to a Private Document (expect 404)

request.description: {{document_id}} is PRIVATE and the member's only grant on it was revoked back in folder 6 - with no access to resolve at all, the endpoint 404s rather than confirming the document exists.

exec: pm.test('private document with no access is a 404', () => pm.response.to.have.status(404));

request.description: Every domain endpoint requires IsAuthenticated globally. This request has no bearer token at all (auth type is explicitly 'No Auth', not just an unset variable).
Project creation is IsOrganizationAdmin-only; the member has org_role=MEMBER.
Blocked by the admin-only permission before it would even reach the self-deactivation check.
The member has EDITOR access on this project (granted in folder 6) - sharing requires OWNER.

exec: pm.test('editor cannot re-share, needs Owner', () => pm.response.to.have.status(403));
pm.test('editor cannot delete, needs Owner', () => pm.response.to.have.status(403));

request.description: Admin is the project's sole OWNER (auto-granted at creation) - the API refuses to let this grant disappear entirely. Rejected before deletion, so the grant is untouched afterward.

exec: pm.test('cannot revoke the only Owner', () => pm.response.to.have.status(400));

item.name: Get Another Org's Project by ID (expect 404, not 403)

request.description: The queryset is scoped to request.user.organization, so a real project belonging to another org is indistinguishable from one that doesn't exist - it never even reveals existence.

exec: pm.test('cross-org fetch is a plain 404, proving tenant isolation', () => pm.response.to.have.status(404));

request.description: Name uniqueness is scoped per-organization; {{project_name}} was already used in folder 4.

exec: pm.test('duplicate project name in same org is rejected', () => pm.response.to.have.status(400));

item.name: Search Projects - No Match (expect 200, empty results)

exec: pm.test('search with no match still returns 200', () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));

item.name: Re-Accept an Already-Used Invitation Token (expect 400, generic message)

request.description: {{invitation_token}} was already consumed in folder 3 - reusing it must fail with the same generic message used for missing/expired tokens (anti-oracle protection).

exec: pm.test('reusing a consumed token is rejected', () => pm.response.to.have.status(400));
pm.test('message does not reveal why', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().token[0]).to.eql('This invitation link is invalid or has expired.'));

request.description: Uses the temp org from the previous request, which has no billing_email set.

request.description: The member has EDITOR (not OWNER) on this project from folder 6 - changing visibility needs the same Owner-only bar as sharing.

exec: pm.test('editor cannot change visibility, needs Owner', () => pm.response.to.have.status(403));

item.name: [As Member/Viewer] Cannot Change Personal Document Visibility (expect 403)

request.description: The member only has VIEWER on this personal document from folder 7.

exec: pm.test('viewer cannot change visibility, needs Owner', () => pm.response.to.have.status(403));

request.description: Soft delete only (is_active=False) — never a hard delete. Admin cannot deactivate self.
Confirms the access-removal actually took effect.

exec: pm.test('deactivated user cannot log in', () => pm.response.to.have.status(401));

request.description: Admin-only. The roster at GET /users/ lists active users only; this is where deactivated ones show up for reactivation.
Admin-only. Reverses a deactivation; an already-active or other-organization user is a 404.

exec: pm.test('member can log in again', () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));

request.description: Admin-only. org_role is ADMIN or MEMBER.
An admin can't change their own role - which also guarantees an organization never loses its last admin.
Soft-deleted documents the caller is Owner of, most recently deleted first - exactly what the restore endpoint lets them bring back.

exec: pm.test('deleted document is in the trash', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().results.map(d => d.id)).to.include(Number(pm.environment.get('document_id'))));

request.description: Requires Owner-level access on the document, not admin-gated like project restore.
Admin-only, like project restore. Every soft-deleted project in the organization, most recently deleted first.

exec: pm.test('deleted project is in the trash', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().results.map(p => p.id)).to.include(Number(pm.environment.get('project_id'))));

request.description: Admin-only, unlike document restore.

item.name: Create Checkout Session (yearly) - optional, just to show the other price

request.description: Optional, run last / skip entirely if short on time. Shows the endpoint works with a different Price (distinct idempotency key, so a genuinely separate Stripe session) - you don't need to complete payment on it. Deliberately placed at the very end, after the subscription is already confirmed active, to avoid adding to the webhook burst right after the first checkout (see the SQLite note in folder 2).

item.name: 13. Throttle Test (run via Collection Runner, 15 iterations, this request only)

request.description: LOGIN_THROTTLE_RATE is 10/min locally. Uses a wrong password on purpose - we only care about request count, not credentials. Run via Collection Runner with iterations=15 selecting ONLY this request; running it inline once in a normal pass just shows 401. Exactly which attempt # flips to 429 depends on whether this email already had recent login attempts within the last minute.

exec: pm.test('not yet throttled (expected on early iterations)', () => pm.response.to.have.status(401));
